ITQAN:v2p373/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p373/r9.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p373/r9.claim: جابوا الصخر means they bored through mountain rock and made houses in it; Umayya’s line is cited as evidence.
ITQAN:v2p373/r9.anchor: قال أخبرني عن قوله تعالى ﴿ جابوا الصخر ﴾ قال نقبوا الحجارة في الجبال فاتخذوها بيوتا

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r3.claim: The surah's historical examples show that God controls individuals and nations, gives respite as He wills, and seizes them when their term ends; none can exceed His limits.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p296/r3.anchor: Similar is His dealing with nations.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r1.claim: The fates of powerful nations prove God's control: after respite, those who cross His limits are seized helplessly despite their power and glory.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p297/r1.anchor: When they wrongly use their freedom to exercise their will and cross the limits set for them by the Almighty, they are given respite

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r1.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r1.claim: God grants nations a wise respite to mend their ways, then seizes them; their destruction anticipates accountability for every person, with full reward or punishment.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r1.anchor: the whole world also will be held accountable one day in which each and every individual will be held responsible for his deeds.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r5.claim: The Thamūd descended from the Ād, inherited their building arts, were also called the second Ād, and carved mountain homes in Wād al-Qurā.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-9-english:p307/r5.anchor: They had carved houses from the mountains of this valley

FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403/r1.author: Abū ʿAlī al-Fārisī
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403/r1.speaker: ابن كثير
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403/r1.claim: Ibn Kathīr retains yāʾ in both connection and pause in يسر and جابوا الصخر.
FARISI-HUJJA:v6p403/r1.anchor: قرأ ابن كثير: يسري* [الفجر/ 4] بالياء وصل أو وقف، وجابوا الصخر بالوادي

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p467/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p467/r3.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p467/r3.claim: Jaba means to pierce, hew, or traverse a land; a poem illustrates crossing a country.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p467/r3.anchor: جاب: خرق وقطع، تقول جبت البلاد أجوبها، إذا قطعتها وجاوزتها

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472/r9.claim: Ibn Wathab reads Thamud with tanwin, unlike the majority; jaba means they hewed the rock to make houses, as in 7:74.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472/r9.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب وثمود بالتنوين. والجمهور: بمنع الصرف. جابوا الصخر

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r1.claim: One report says Thamud first hewed mountains, rock, and marble and built 1,700 stone cities in Wadi al-Qura; another says they cut their valley or brought water through cleft stone.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p472#2/r1.anchor: أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام ثمود، وبنوا ألفا وسبعمائة مدينة

MAJAZ:v2p297/r7.author: Abū ʿUbayda Maʿmar b. al-Muthannā
MAJAZ:v2p297/r7.speaker: author
MAJAZ:v2p297/r7.claim: Jābū al-ṣakhr means they pierced the rocks; jāba al-falāt means entering and crossing the desert.
MAJAZ:v2p297/r7.anchor: «جابوا الصخر» (9) نقبوا، ويجوب الفلاة أيضا يدخل فيها ويقطعها

JISHUMI:v10p7395/r1.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r1.speaker: أبي بن كعب
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r1.claim: A report from the Prophet promises forgiveness to one who recites al-Fajr and a light on the Resurrection Day to one who recites it daily.
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r1.anchor: وعن أبي بن كعب، عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: من قرأ سورة (الفجر) غفر له

JISHUMI:v10p7395/r2.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r2.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r2.claim: After the previous chapter said that all creatures return to God and He judges them, this chapter emphasizes that He watches over them, warning and encouraging them.
JISHUMI:v10p7395/r2.anchor: ولما ختم السورة المتقدمة بأن مصير الخلق إليه وحسابهم عليه، افتتح هذه السورة بتأكيد ذلك بالقسم

MUQATIL:89:1-10/r5.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:89:1-10/r5.speaker: author
MUQATIL:89:1-10/r5.claim: Thamud are Salih's people; they hollowed out the largest mountains into houses with stone doors and locks, as also described in 26:149.

TABRISI:89:1-30#6/r5.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#6/r5.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:1-30#6/r5.claim: Thamud cut through and hollowed rock in the valley where they lived, Wadi al-Qura.
TABRISI:89:1-30#6/r5.anchor: أي وكيف فعل بثمود الذين قطعوا الصخر ونقبوها بالوادي الذي كانوا ينزلونه

TABRISI:89:1-30#6/r6.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:1-30#6/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
TABRISI:89:1-30#6/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says they carved houses from mountains, as the Quran says they hewed houses from the mountains.
TABRISI:89:1-30#6/r6.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانوا ينحتون الجبال فيجعلون منها بيوتا

BURSEVI:v10p329/r5.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p329/r5.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p329/r5.claim: Thamud were an Arab tribe descended from Thamud, brother of Jadis, living at al-Hijr between the Hijaz and Tabuk, worshipping idols like Aad, and known as the people of Salih.
BURSEVI:v10p329/r5.anchor: عطف على عاد وثمود قبيلة مشهورة سميت باسم جدهم ثمود

BURSEVI:v10p329/r6.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p329/r6.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v10p329/r6.claim: They cut into hard mountain stone to make dwellings in the Valley of al-Qura near Medina; the verse's word for valley drops its final yāʾ, and the word for cutting also gives the name of a shirt pocket. They may have built 1,700 stone towns.
BURSEVI:v10p329/r6.anchor: والمراد هنا هو وادي القرى بالقرب من المدينة الشريفة من جهة الشأن

BURSEVI:v10p329/r7.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v10p329/r7.speaker: أبو نضرة
BURSEVI:v10p329/r7.claim: Abu Nadra reports that the Prophet passed through the Valley of Thamud during the Tabuk expedition on a grey horse and ordered the party to hurry because it was a cursed valley.
BURSEVI:v10p329/r7.anchor: قال أبو نضرة أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزوة تبوك على وادي ثمود

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3426#2/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3426#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3426#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Thamud carved houses in the mountains and Pharaoh's stakes were the troops who established his rule.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3426#2/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : جابوا الصخر بالواد قال : كانوا ينحتون من الجبال بيوتا وفرعون ذي الاوتاد قال الاوتاد الجنود

IBNABIHATIM:v10p3426#3/r1.author: Ibn Abī Ḥātim al-Rāzī
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3426#3/r1.speaker: مجاهد
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3426#3/r1.claim: Mujahid says Thamud burned or hollowed mountains into houses, Pharaoh fixed people with stakes, and the scourge was the punishment they suffered.
IBNABIHATIM:v10p3426#3/r1.anchor: عن مجاهد جابوا الصخر قال : حرقوا الجبال فجعلوها بيوتا وفرعون ذي الاوتاد قال : كان يتد الناس بالاوتاد

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r1.claim: The historical lessons either constitute evidence for an omitted oath-answer, or precede “Your Lord is indeed watching” to build suspense and prepare the audience for that answer.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r1.anchor: فهذه العبر جزئيات من مضمون جواب القسم ، فإن كان محذوفا فذكرها دليله ، وإن كان الجواب قوله : { إن ربك لبالمرصاد }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r4.claim: ʿAd and Thamud open the warning because they were familiar; Pharaoh follows because Arabs knew Moses' mission to him through the region's scriptural communities.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p317/r4.anchor: وقد ابتدئت الموعظة بذكر عاد وثمود لشهرتهما بين المخاطبين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r1.claim: Thamud is diptote as the name of a known people; masculine plural “who carved” treats the tribe as a people rather than using feminine agreement.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r1.anchor: ومنع { ثمود } من الصرف لأن المراد به الأمة المعروفة ، ووصف باسم الموصول لجمع المذكر

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r2.claim: Jābū means cut or carve: Thamud hollowed rocks for homes, as another verse says; some say they were humanity's first stone and marble carvers.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r2.anchor: ومعنى { جابوا } : قطعوا ، أي نحتوا الصخر واتخذوا فيه بيوتا كما قال تعالى : { وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r3.claim: Ṣakhr means large stones; a wād is low land between two mountains and also a channel for much water, with forms ending in dāl or yāʾ.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r3.anchor: و { الصخر } : الحجارة العظيمة . والواد : اسم لأرض كائنة بين جبلين منخفضة

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r4.claim: Most read the valley name without final yāʾ; Ibn Kathir and Yaqub keep it in both positions, while Warsh from Nafi keeps it only in connection, following cadence.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r4.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بدون ياء . وقرأه ابن كثير ويعقوب بياء في آخره وصلا ووقفا

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r5.claim: The valley is the established home of Thamud, also called Wadi al-Qura and al-Hijr; it lies between Khaybar and Tayma on the Medina-to-Syria route and was later inhabited by Jews and Arab tribes.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r5.anchor: والواد : علم بالغلبة على منازل ثمود ، ويقال له : وادي القرى ، بإضافته إلى ( القرى )

IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r6.claim: The Prophet campaigned there and conquered it in year seven; local Arabs accepted Islam and Jews made a tax agreement. The bāʾ means location.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v30p320/r6.anchor: وكان غزاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفتحه سنة سبع فأسلم من فيه من العرب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r4.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r4.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads Thamud with nunation on the dāl.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r4.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب «وثمودا» بتنوين الدال

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r5.speaker: جمهور المفسرين
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r5.claim: They explain that Thamud excavated rock to make homes in their valleys; a valley may mean the space between two mountains even without water.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r5.anchor: وجابوا الصخر معناه خرقوه ونحتوه، وكانوا في أوديتهم قد نحتوا بيوتهم في حجارة،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r6.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r6.claim: Al-Tha'labi says the verse means the Valley of al-Qura.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r7.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r7.claim: Some instead say they cut through their valley and brought water through rock they split, evidence of strength and ambition.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r7.anchor:
وقال قوم:
المعنى جابوا واديهم وجلبوا ماءهم في صخر شقوه، وهذا فعل ذوي القوة والآمال،

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r8.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r8.speaker: ابن كثير والجمهور ونافع
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r8.claim: Ibn Kathir reads the final yāʾ in bil-wādi; most of the seven omit it, and Nafi differs in transmission.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p478/r8.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير «بالوادي» بياء، وقرأ أكثر السبعة «بالواد» دون ياء واختلف في ذلك نافع،

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117/r1.claim: Thamūd cut and hollowed out rock; Isḥāq identifies the valley as Wādī al-Qurā.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117/r1.anchor: قطعوه ونقبوه قال إسحاق والوادي وادي القرى

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117/r2.speaker: الحسن
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117/r2.claim: Al-Ḥasan reads bi-l-wādī with the yāʾ retained in both forms.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v9p117/r2.anchor: وقرأ الحسن بالوادي بإثبات الياء في الحالين

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r1.speaker: ابن جرير
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r1.claim: Ibn Jarir allows that Iram could be either a tribe or a town inhabited by Aad, which would explain its indeclinable form; Ibn Kathir thinks the context concerns the tribe.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r1.anchor: وقول ابن جرير: يحتمل أن يكون المراد بقوله: {إرم} قبيلة أو بلدة كانت عاد تسكنها فلذلك لم تصرف فيه نظر؛

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r2.claim: They say Thamud cut through rock in the valley, carving or boring into it; the same root appears in terms for cutting through clothing and an opening in a garment.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس: ينحتونها ويخرقونها. وكذا قال مجاهد، وقتادة، والضحاك، وابن زيد.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r3.claim: The cited phrase about cutting through clothing and the verse from al-Shuʿara about carving houses from mountains illustrate the lexical sense of boring through rock.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r3.anchor: ومنه يقال: "مجتابي النمار". إذا خرقوها، واجتاب الثوب: إذا فتحه. ومنه الجيب أيضا.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r4.claim: Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim cite poetry describing sturdy people striking hard rocks with strong arms as evidence for the verse's image.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r4.anchor: ألا كل شيء -ما خلا الله-بائد … كما باد حي من شنيف ومارد

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r5.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r5.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Thamud were Arabs whose home was Wadi al-Qura; the account of Aad was already given at length in al-Aʿraf.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v8p396#2/r5.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق: كانوا عربا، وكان منزلهم بوادي القرى.

FARRA:v3p261/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p261/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p261/r1.claim: Jābū al-ṣakhr means they bored through the rock and made houses in it.
FARRA:v3p261/r1.anchor:
وقوله عز وجل: جابوا الصخر (9) خرقوا الصخر، فاتخذوه بيوتا.
وقوله عز

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p526#6/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p526#6/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p526#6/r1.claim: Jābū al-ṣakhr means they bored through the rock and made houses from it.

JISHUMI:v10p7400/r12.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7400/r12.speaker: مجاهد
JISHUMI:v10p7400/r12.claim: Mujāhid says the Thamūd cut rock, or cut mountains into houses; they lived in their valley or Wādī al-Qurā, built structures there, and were said to be first to carve stone.
JISHUMI:v10p7400/r12.anchor: قوم صالح الذين جابوا قيل: قطعوا الصخر وقيل: قطعوا الجبال بيوتا

JISHUMI:v10p7403/r9.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r9.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r9.claim: The accusative of aklan is an absolute object and lammā modifies the eating.
JISHUMI:v10p7403/r9.anchor: أكلا نصب على المصدر وهو المفعول المطلق، ولما نعت للأكل

KASHSHAF:89:9/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:9/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF:89:9/r1.claim: Thamud cut dwellings into mountain rock, as in the cited verse.
KASHSHAF:89:9/r1.anchor: قطعوا صخر الجبال واتخذوا فيها بيوتاً

KASHSHAF:89:9/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF:89:9/r2.speaker: قيل
KASHSHAF:89:9/r2.claim: They were said to be the first to carve mountains, rock, and marble, and to have built 1,700 stone cities.
KASHSHAF:89:9/r2.anchor: قيل : أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p750#2/r8.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p750#2/r8.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p750#2/r8.claim: Jabou al-sakhr means they cut mountain rock and made homes in it; another report says Thamud first carved mountains and built 1,700 stone cities.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p750#2/r8.anchor: قطعوا صخر الجبال واتخذوا فيها بيوتا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r15.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r15.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r15.claim: One reading says Thamud cut and hollowed out rock to make houses, as 26:149 also says.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r15.anchor: حتى جعلوه بيوتا , كما قال تعالى : { وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r16.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r16.speaker: الشاعر
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r16.claim: The cited poem describes striking a solid rock with strong arms, supporting the reading that Thamud hewed stone.
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r16.anchor: وهم ضربوا في كل صماء صعدة … بأيد شديد

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r17.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r17.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p267/r17.claim: Another reading says they traveled around the valley to obtain stone.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p269/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p269/r1.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p269/r1.claim: He identifies the wadi as Wadi al-Qura.

MAWARDI-FULL:v6p269/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p269/r2.speaker: أبو الأشهب عن أبي نضرة
MAWARDI-FULL:v6p269/r2.claim: They report that during the Tabuk campaign the Prophet passed through the valley of Thamud on a gray horse and ordered the group to hurry because it was cursed.

NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#2/r1.claim: Thamud cut houses into mountain rock; a report says they were the first to hollow mountains and built 1,700 stone cities; the valley is Wadi al-Qura.
NASAFI-FULL:v4p337#2/r1.anchor: قطعوا صخر الجبال واتخذوا فيها بيوتا قيل أول من تحت الجبال والصخور ثمود وبنوا ألفا

QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r1.claim: Thamud are the people of Salih; jābū means they cut through or traversed, as in the verb for traveling through lands, and the word for a shirt pocket also derives from cutting.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r1.anchor: ثمود: هم قوم صالح. و { جابوا }: قطعوا. ومنه: فلان يجوب البلاد

QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r2.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r2.claim: A poet's lines about Ibn al-Zubayr's gift of sixty loads use jābat to mean a camel traversed a land.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r2.anchor: ما إن رأيت قلوصا قبلها حملت ستين وسقا ولا جابت به بلدا

QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r3.speaker: المفسرون
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r3.claim: They say Thamud first carved mountains, figures, and marble, making 1,700 stone cities and 2.7 million stone dwellings; 15:82 also describes their rock-cut homes.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r3.anchor: قال المفسرون: أول من نحت الجبال والصور والرخام: ثمود

QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r4.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r4.claim: He identifies the valley as Wadi al-Qura.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r4.anchor: { بالواد } أي بوادي القرى قاله محمد بن إسحاق

QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r5.speaker: أبو نضرة
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r5.claim: He reports that the Prophet passed through the valley of Thamud during Tabuk and ordered the company to hurry because it was a cursed valley.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r5.anchor: أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم في غزاة تبوك على وادي ثمود

QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r6.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r6.claim: Others describe the valley as a passage between mountains where Thamud carved homes, dwellings, and pools; generally it is any gap between hills that carries runoff or gives passage.
QURTUBI-FULL:89:9/r6.anchor: وقيل: الوادي بين جبال، وكانوا ينقبون في تلك الجبال بيوتا ودورا وأحواضا

NAHHAS:v5p221/r2.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p221/r2.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p221/r2.claim: Thamūd is genitive; as a tribal name it is indeclinable, while declension treats it as the name of the people. The tanwīn may be omitted to avoid two adjacent sukūns.
NAHHAS:v5p221/r2.anchor: في موضع خفض والتقدير وبثمود لم ينصرف لأنه اسم للقبيلة ومن صرفه جعله اسما للحي

NAHHAS:v5p221/r3.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p221/r3.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p221/r3.claim: Alladhīna may be a genitive adjective, an accusative meaning I mean, or nominative meaning they are the ones who cut through rock.
NAHHAS:v5p221/r3.anchor: ( الذين ) في موضع خفض على النعت ويجوز أن يكون في موضع نصب بمعنى أعني وفي موضع رفع بمعنى هم

NAHHAS:v5p221/r4.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v5p221/r4.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v5p221/r4.claim: Jābū derives from the hollow verb jāba yājūbu, to cut through something and enter it; the yāʾ is omitted at the verse ending, its kasra signaling it.
NAHHAS:v5p221/r4.anchor: وجابوا من ذوات الواو جاب الشيء يجوبه إذا قطعه ودخل فيه وحذفت الياء من الواو لأنه رأس آية

QUTB-ZILAL:89:9/r1.author: Sayyid Quṭb
QUTB-ZILAL:89:9/r1.speaker: author
QUTB-ZILAL:89:9/r1.claim: Thamud lived at al-Hijr in northern Arabia and cut rock to build palaces and carve mountain shelters and caves.

RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r16.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r16.speaker: الليث
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r16.claim: Al-Layth explains jābū as cutting through something, by analogy with cutting a garment opening.
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r16.anchor: فقال الليث : الجواب قطعك الشيء كما يجاب الجيب يقال جاب يجوب جوبا

RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r17.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r17.speaker: الفراء
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r17.claim: Al-Farrāʾ adds the form yajību, and explains jābū al-bilād as traveling through and traversing lands.
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r17.anchor: وزاد الفراء يجيب جيبا ويقال : جبت البلاد جوبا أي جلت فيها وقطعتها

RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r18.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r18.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r18.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Thamūd cut through the land to make houses, basins, and other buildings, as in 7:74.
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r18.anchor: قال ابن عباس : يجوبون البلاد فيجعلون منها بيوتا وأحواضا وما أرادوا من الأبنية

RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r19.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r19.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r19.claim: A report says the Thamūd were the first to carve mountains, stone, and marble, making 1,700 stone cities.
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r19.anchor: قيل : أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام / ثمود ، وبنوا ألفا وسبعمائة مدينة كلها من الحجارة

RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r20.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r20.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI-FULL:v31p152/r20.claim: Muqātil identifies the valley as Wādī al-Qurā.

SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r1.claim: The common reading declines Thamūd, while Ibn Waththāb declines it; alladhīna can be attached or detached on the same analyses as the preceding relative.
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r1.anchor: قرأ العامة بمنع الصرف، وابن وثاب بصرفه.

SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r2.claim: Jāba means cut or pierce an object and jāba al-bilād means traverse lands; the quoted line uses the latter.
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r2.anchor: وجاب الشيء يجوبه قطعه وخرقه جوبا. وجبت البلاد: قطعتها سيرا.

SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r3.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r3.speaker: الشاعر
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r3.claim: The verse's verb jābat attests traversing a country by camel.
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r3.anchor: قال الشاعر: 4563 ولا رأيت قلوصا قبلها حملت

SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r4.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r4.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r4.claim: Bi-l-wādī may attach to jābū, meaning they carved there, or to an omitted circumstantial phrase describing the rock or the agents.
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r4.anchor: قوله: { بالواد } متعلق: إما ب " جابوا " ، أي: فيه

SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r5.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r5.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r5.claim: Ibn Kathīr and Warsh retain yāʾ in al-wādī in both contexts; Qunbul has both-positions and connected-only reports, while others delete it to match the muṣḥaf and rhyme, as at 89:4.
SAMIN-DURR:89:9/r5.anchor: وأثبت ياء " الوادي " في الحالين ابن كثير وورش، بخلاف عن قنبل

STUDYQURAN:89:9/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:89:9/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:89:9/r1.claim: Thamūd were a pre-Islamic northern Arabian tribe who rejected the Prophet Ṣāliḥ; their account is related elsewhere.
STUDYQURAN:89:9/r1.anchor: a pre-Islamic northern Arabian tribe who rejected the Prophet Ṣāliḥ

TAB-FULL:v24p369/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r1.claim: The Thamūd cut into rock and made houses inside it, as in the verse about carving secure homes in mountains; jāb means to enter and cut through.
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r1.anchor: وقوله: {وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد} يقول: وبثمود الذي خرقوا الصخر ودخلوه، فاتخذوه بيوتا

TAB-FULL:v24p369/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r2.speaker: النابغة
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r2.claim: Al-Nābigha’s verse uses jawaba for entering and traversing, supporting the meaning of jābū.
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r2.anchor: ومنه قول نابغة: [البحر الطويل] أتاك أبو ليلى يجوب به الدجى … دجى الليل جواب الفلاة عميم

TAB-FULL:v24p369/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says the Thamūd broke through the rock and carved homes from mountains.
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس، في قوله: {وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد} يقول: فخرقوها

TAB-FULL:v24p369/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r4.speaker: مجاهد
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r4.claim: Mujāhid says they cut through the mountains and made homes inside them.
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد} قال: جابوا الجبال، فجعلوها بيوتا

TAB-FULL:v24p369/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r5.speaker: قتادة
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r5.claim: Qatāda says they cut and hollowed the rock into houses; another report describes them drilling through it.
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r5.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد} جابوها ونحتوها بيوتا

TAB-FULL:v24p369/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r6.speaker: الضحاك
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r6.claim: Al-Ḍaḥḥāk glosses the expression as cutting through stones.
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r6.anchor: سمعت الضحاك، يقول في قوله: {جابوا الصخر بالواد} يقول: قدوا الحجارة

TAB-FULL:v24p369/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r7.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r7.claim: Ibn Zayd says they struck dwellings into mountain rock and made homes within it.
TAB-FULL:v24p369/r7.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد} : ضربوا البيوت والمساكن في الصخر في الجبال

TABATABAI:89:9-15/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:89:9-15/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:89:9-15/r4.claim: The verb jāb means to cut: the people of Thamūd cut into mountain rock to make homes, as in another verse.
TABATABAI:89:9-15/r4.anchor: الجوب القطع أي قطعوا صخر الجبال بنحتها بيوتا

TABRISI:89:29/r4.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:89:29/r4.speaker: author
TABRISI:89:29/r4.claim: Jawwāb means one who traverses widely or a person who travels the desert forcefully; the poet describes such a traveler.
TABRISI:89:29/r4.anchor: والجواب القطع قال النابغة: أتاك أبو ليلى تجوب به الدجى

THALABI:v10p197/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p197/r2.speaker: author
THALABI:v10p197/r2.claim: Thamūd cut and hollowed out rock in Wādī al-Qurā, carving houses from mountains as in 7:74.
THALABI:v10p197/r2.anchor: وثمود أي وثمود الذين جابوا قطعوا وخرقوا الصخر الحجر

THALABI:v10p197/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p197/r3.speaker: أهل السير
THALABI:v10p197/r3.claim: Historians say Thamūd were the first to carve mountains, rock, and marble and built two million seven hundred thousand stone houses.
THALABI:v10p197/r3.anchor: قال أهل السير: أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام ثمود، فبنوا من الدور والمنازل

THALABI:v10p197/r4.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v10p197/r4.speaker: أبو جعفر
THALABI:v10p197/r4.claim: Abū Jaʿfar, Abū Ḥātim, and Warsh retain the yāʾ of al-wādī in liaison; Ibn Kathīr by al-Bazzī and al-ʿAwwāsh and Yaʿqūb retain it in liaison and pause, while others drop it as a verse ending.
THALABI:v10p197/r4.anchor: وأثبت أبو جعفر وأبو حاتم وورش الياء في الوادي وصلا

ASAD-NOTES:89:6#n6/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:89:6#n6/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:89:6#n6/r1.claim: The valley is Wadi al-Qura, north of Medina on the old caravan route from South Arabia to Syria; Asad points to notes on 7:56 and 7:59.
ASAD-NOTES:89:6#n6/r1.anchor: The "valley" referred to in the sequence is the Wadi 'l-Qura, situated north of Medina

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r1.claim: Thamud dug through and cut the rock.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r1.anchor: {وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد} أي نقبوها وقطعوها.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r2.speaker: الليث، الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r2.claim: The root “jawb” means cutting through; al-Farra gives a related verb and cites a poetic line with “tajibu.”
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r2.anchor: الليث: الجوب: قطعك الشيء كما يجاب، جاب يجوب جوبا

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r3.claim: They carved mountains into houses, pools, and other buildings, as also stated in 26:149.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس: كانوا يجوبون الجبال، فيجعلون منها بيوتا، وأحواضا،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r4.speaker: الفراء
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r4.claim: They pierced the rock and made houses in it.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v23p503#2/r4.anchor: وقال الفراء: خرقوا الصخر فاتخذوه بيوتا

WAHIDI-QT:89:9/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-QT:89:9/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-QT:89:9/r1.claim: Thamud cut rock to make dwellings in the Wadi al-Qura, where they lived.
WAHIDI-QT:89:9/r1.anchor: { وثمود الذين جابوا } قطعوا { الصخر } فاتخذوا منها البيوت { بالواد } يعني وادي القرى وكانت مساكنهم هناك

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:7-10/r6.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:7-10/r6.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:7-10/r6.claim: Thamud cut rock into houses in the valley, identified as Wadi al-Qura, where they lived.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:89:7-10/r6.anchor: قطعوا { الصخر } فاتخذوا منها البيوت { بالواد } يعني: وادي القرى، وكانت مساكنهم هناك.

ELMALILI:89:9/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:9/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:9/r1.claim: The Thamud cut rock in the valley to build their houses; this power and craft were gifts God gave them.
ELMALILI:89:9/r1.anchor: Bu suretle kendilerine evler yapıyorlardı ki bu Allah’ın onlara vermiş olduğu bir kuvvet ve san‘at idi

ELMALILI:89:9/r2.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:9/r2.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:9/r2.claim: The verb javb means cutting through something as if slicing it, and it can also mean traversing a distance.
ELMALILI:89:9/r2.anchor: “Cevb” bir şeyi yaka biçer gibi kesip biçmektir. Mesafe kat‘etmeye de “cevb” tâbir olunur

ELMALILI:89:9/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:9/r3.speaker: İbn Abbas
ELMALILI:89:9/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas says they traveled through lands and carved houses, pools, and buildings to their liking from mountains and rocks.
ELMALILI:89:9/r3.anchor: İbn Abbas demiştir ki: “Beldeleri dolaşırlar ve

ELMALILI:89:9/r4.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:9/r4.speaker: Mukātil
ELMALILI:89:9/r4.claim: Muqatil identifies the valley as Wadi al-Qura.

ELMALILI:89:9/r5.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:9/r5.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:9/r5.claim: One report says the Thamud were the first to carve mountains, rocks, and marble, making about 1,700 cities, all of stone.
ELMALILI:89:9/r5.anchor: bin yedi yüz kadar medine yapmışlardı, hepsi taştan idi

ELMALILI:89:9/r6.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:9/r6.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:9/r6.claim: Another report says they cut channels in their valley and directed water into a reservoir carved inside a rock.
ELMALILI:89:9/r6.anchor: vâdilerini kesmişler, sularını yonttukları bir kayanın içine mahzen hâlinde celbetmişlerdi

ELMALILI:89:9/r7.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:9/r7.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:9/r7.claim: Genealogists identify Thamud as a famous extinct Arab tribe and offer differing ancestry traditions; the commentator leaves the genealogy uncertain.
ELMALILI:89:9/r7.anchor: Nessâbûnun zikrettikleri bu neseb, sahih olsun olmasın

ELMALILI:89:9/r8.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:89:9/r8.speaker: author
ELMALILI:89:9/r8.claim: The Thamud’s known homes were at al-Hijr between Syria and the Hijaz, and their destruction is recounted in multiple surahs.
ELMALILI:89:9/r8.anchor: Areb’de Semûd ve Şam ile Hicaz arasında Hicr’de menzilleri mâruftur

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r1.claim: Pre-Islamic poetry names ʿĀd and Ṯamūd and sometimes hints at their destruction, but rarely specifies how; Quran's brief allusions therefore presume listeners knew the stories in outline.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Zwar werden beide Namen in einer ganzen Reihe von Versen erwähnt, von denen einige auch auf den Untergang der beiden Völkerschaften anspielen, doch wird die Art und Weise ihrer Vernichtung nicht näher spezifiziert.

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r2.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r2.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r2.claim: The likely authentic poem of Umayya b. Abī ṣ-Ṣalt differs from the Quranic Thamūd account: no divinely sent warner is disobeyed; instead the dead she-camel's calf curses the people.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r2.anchor: Es fehlt die Figur eines göttlich gesandten Warners, dessen expliziten Anweisungen die Ṯamūd zuwider handeln; stattdessen geht die Vernichtung der Ṯamūd auf einen durch das Junge des getöteten Kamels ausgestoßenen Fluch zurück

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r3.claim: Aḥmar is linked to ʿĀd in Zuhair's Muʿallaqa and another poem, unlike Umayya's Thamūd story; this may mean the she-camel story shifted between peoples or their names were partly interchangeable.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Interessant ist, dass der von Umayya für die Tötung der von Gott zu den Ṯamūd gesandten Kamelstute verantwortlich gemachte Aḥmar in der Muʿallaqa des Zuhair und einem weiteren Gedicht nicht den Ṯamūd, sondern den ʿĀd zugeordnet wird

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r4.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r4.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r4.claim: An early Zuhair verse lists Pharaoh among figures God destroyed, resembling Quranic punishment catalogues of historical actors, though Zuhair lists individuals rather than collectives; Quranic cycles may develop related ideas.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r4.anchor: Offensichtlich hat man es hier mit einer koranischen Straflisten durchaus vergleichbaren Zusammenstellung geschichtlicher Akteure zu tun (bei Zuhair sind es allerdings Individuen und keine Kollektive)

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r5.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r5.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r5.claim: Together with brief accounts in 85:17–18, 73:15–16, and 91:11–15, these references form the nucleus of the Quran's later-expanded punishment-story repertoire; sura 105 is an earlier but different kind of narrative.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-13:anmerkung/r5.anchor: Neben der vorliegenden Sure finden sich in Gruppe II der frühmekkanischen Suren nur noch drei weitere narrativ geprägte Abschnitte

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:9:anmerkung/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:9:anmerkung/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:9:anmerkung/r1.claim: The verse and later parallels describe tombs cut into rock at al-Ḥiǧr, later Madāʾin Ṣāliḥ, and another cited poem locates the Thamūd there.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:9:anmerkung/r1.anchor: Der Vers spielt wie die späteren Stellen 7:74, 15:82 und 26:149

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:10:anmerkung/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:10:anmerkung/r3.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:10:anmerkung/r3.claim: The architectural reading of Pharaoh's pegs gains support from the sura's association of ʿĀd and Thamūd with impressive building projects.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:10:anmerkung/r3.anchor: Für Horovitz’ Deutung der ʾautād spricht, dass die vorliegende Sure auch die ʿĀd und Ṯamūd mit besonderen architektonischen Leistungen in Verbindung bringt

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-14:kommentar/r1.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-14:kommentar/r1.speaker: author
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-14:kommentar/r1.claim: All three peoples are tied to monumental building; these works suggest human attempts at self-perpetuation that remain futile before God's punishment, recalling Babel and the root ḫ-l-d for striving to endure.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-14:kommentar/r1.anchor: Es liegt nahe, die Pointe dieser Verweise darin zu erblicken, dass die betreffenden Bauwerke

CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-14:kommentar/r3.author: Nicolai Sinai (Frühmekkanische Suren), with Nora K. Schmid, using preparatory work by Angelika Neuwirth; later parts Dirk Hartwig, Angelika Neuwirth et al. (author line per sura in segments)
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-14:kommentar/r3.speaker: Labīd
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-14:kommentar/r3.claim: Labīd's poem presents humans as transient while stars, mountains, and towers endure; the Quran passage stresses that even apparently permanent mountains are ultimately fragile.
CORPUSCORANICUM:89:6-14:kommentar/r3.anchor: Wir vergehen; unvergänglich sind die Sterne am Himmel

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r1.claim: The destroyed peoples show later generations that material strength cannot avert divine punishment for denial and rebellion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r1.anchor: geçmişte bazı toplulukların inkâr ve azgınlıkları yüzünden nasıl helâk edildiklerine, maddî güç ve imkânları olsa da bunların kendilerini ilâhî cezadan kurtaramadığına dikkat çekilmekte

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r5.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r5.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r5.claim: Thamud met the same fate because they accused their prophet Salih of lying (7:73–78; 11:61–68; 68:4–5).
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r5.anchor: Semûd kavmi de, kendilerine gönderilen Sâlih peygamberi yalancılıkla itham ettikleri için aynı âkıbete uğramıştır

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r7.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r7.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r7.claim: The first audience likely knew these peoples’ stories by hearsay or had seen or heard of their ruins; their recurring traits were great strength and unrestrained corruption and rebellion.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:89:6/r7.anchor: Bu âyetlerde söz konusu edilen kavimlerin iki özelliğine dikkat çekildiği görülmektedir: İlki çok güçlü olmaları, ikincisi de ülkelerinde azgınlığa sapmaları

QIRAAT-ER:89:9:7#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:89:9:7#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:89:9:7#1/r1.claim: The reading restores or pronounces final yāʾ in al-wādī, lengthening the word without changing root or syntax.
QIRAAT-ER:89:9:7#1/r1.anchor: restores or pronounces final yāʾ in al-wādī, lengthening the valley word

QIRAAT-ER:89:9:7#2/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:89:9:7#2/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:89:9:7#2/r1.claim: The pause and continuation forms shorten al-wād at pause and pronounce al-wādī in continuation, making final yāʾ recitation-sensitive.
QIRAAT-ER:89:9:7#2/r1.anchor: Canonical pause/continuation form shows a waqf-like shortened al-wād followed by al-wādī

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p370#4/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p370#4/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p370#4/r1.claim: Qatāda glosses their hewing of rock as boring and carving it.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p370#4/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله ﴿ جابوا الصخر بالواد ﴾ قال نقبوا الصخر نحتوا الصخر

ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r1.claim: Thamud is a well-known tribe named for its ancestor, brother of Jadis, descended through ʿAbir, Iram, and Sam from Noah; they were Arab peoples living at al-Hijr between the Hijaz and Tabuk and worshipped idols.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r1.anchor: وثمود عطف على عاد وهي قبيلة مشهورة سميت باسم جدهم ثمود أخي جديس وهما عابر بن إرم

ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r2.claim: The name is indeclinable as a proper feminine name; Ibn Waththab declines it when it denotes the people, and it may be Arabic from “little water” or foreign, as al-Raghib relates.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r2.anchor: ومنع الصرف للعلمية والتأنيث وقرأ ابن وثاب بالتنوين صرفه باعتبار الحي

ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r3.claim: “They cut the rock” means cutting mountain rock and hollowing homes in it, as in 7:74; a report says Thamud first carved stone and built 1,700 stone cities, which al-Alusi doubts.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r3.anchor: الذين جابوا الصخر أي قطعوا صخر الجبال واتخذوا فيها بيوتا نحتوها من الصخر كقوله تعالى وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r4.claim: The valley is Wadi al-Qura; the reading with yāʾ and the preposition may attach to the verb or function as a circumstantial phrase.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r4.anchor: بالواد هو وادي القرى وقريء بالياء آخر الحروف والباء للظرفية والجار والمجرور متعلق بجابوا

ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r5.claim: Some construe the preposition as instrument or cause: they cut the rock with or because of their valley, making it a water-place; al-Alusi says this is less apparent.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r5.anchor: أي جابوا الصخر بواديهم أو بسببه

ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r6.claim: The primary sense of jābū is literally to cut through; a cited poetic line uses the verb of traversing a land, while al-Raghib derives “answer” from cutting a hollow through speech.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r6.anchor: قال الشاعر ولا رأيت قلوصاقبلها حملت

ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r7.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r7.claim: Al-Raghib derives “answer” from cutting through a hollow in the earth, then extends it to crossing any land and to the reply that completes a question.
ALUSI-FULL:v30p124/r7.anchor: وقال الراغب الجواب قطع الجوبة وهي الغائط من الأرض ثم يستعمل في قطع كل أرض

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p418#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p418#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p418#2/r1.claim: Thamud cut stone in the valley, carving homes into mountains; the valley is identified as Wadi al-Qura.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p418#2/r1.anchor: أي: وبثمود، {الذين جابوا الصخر} قطعوا الحجر، واحدتها: صخرة، {بالواد} يعني [وادي القرى] (4)

BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p418#2/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p418#2/r2.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب وورش
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p418#2/r2.claim: Ibn Kathir and Yaʿqub retain the yāʾ in al-wadi in both pause and connection; Warsh retains it only in connection, while the others omit it.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v8p418#2/r2.anchor: وأثبت ابن كثير ويعقوب الياء في الوادي وصلا ووقفا على الأصل، وأثبتها ورش وصلا

BAYDAWI-FULL:89:9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:9/r1.claim: Thamūd cut rock and made homes in it, as 26:149 says they carved houses from mountains; the valley is Wādī al-Qurā.
BAYDAWI-FULL:89:9/r1.anchor: قطعوه واتخذوه منازل لقوله: { وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا }

BINTSHATI:v2p138/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p138/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p138/r6.claim: The Qur'an cites ʿĀd, Iram, Thamūd, and Pharaoh for the moral lesson, whereas exegetes have filled in details on which they disagree widely.
BINTSHATI:v2p138/r6.anchor: وقد أكثر المفسرون في الكلام عن عاد إرم ذات العماد، وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد، وفرعون ذي الأوتاد

BINTSHATI:v2p140/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p140/r2.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI:v2p140/r2.claim: One explanation says the Thamūd carved houses from rock; al-Rāzī reports that they were first to carve mountains and built 1,700 stone cities.
BINTSHATI:v2p140/r2.anchor: وقد كانت ثمود أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام، وبنوا ألفاً وسبعمائة مدينة

BINTSHATI:v2p140/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p140/r3.speaker: بعضهم
BINTSHATI:v2p140/r3.claim: Other explanations take jābū as crossing the valley, or splitting rock to make a water-storage valley; Muḥammad ʿAbduh sees this as evidence of their strength and understanding.
BINTSHATI:v2p140/r3.anchor: وقيل: إنهم شقوا الصخر واتخذوه وادياً يخزنون فيه الماء

BINTSHATI:v2p141/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p141/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p141/r5.claim: The author rejects the accumulated details as foreign to Qur'anic style: it deliberately omits minor particulars and directs attention to the fate of tyrants; much is intrusive Israelite lore.
BINTSHATI:v2p141/r5.anchor: وفي منهجنا أن كل هذه التأويلات تحمل القرآن الكريم ما ليس من بيانه وطبيعته

BINTSHATI:v2p142/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p142/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p142/r2.claim: They rejected Hūd and the messengers, denied God and His signs, and rebelled arrogantly.
BINTSHATI:v2p142/r2.anchor: فكذبوه {قَالُوا يَا هُودُ مَا جِئْتَنَا بِبَيِّنَةٍ

BINTSHATI:v2p143/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p143/r5.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p143/r5.claim: Thamūd are also an ancient Arab people, later than Hūd's ʿĀd according to the Qur'anic sequence; the Qur'an mentions them 26 times to warn about disbelief and tyranny.

BINTSHATI:v2p144/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r1.claim: The Qur'an's account identifies Thamūd as the people of Ṣāliḥ, who called them to worship God alone; they rejected him and hamstrung the forbidden she-camel.
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r1.anchor: وجوهر قصتهم فيما نتلو من آيات الكتاب المحكم أنهم قوم صالح عليه السلام

BINTSHATI:v2p144/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r2.claim: Thamūd chose blindness over guidance and were destroyed by the overwhelming blast or thunderbolt, while God rescued Ṣāliḥ and the believers and left the wrongdoers prostrate.

BINTSHATI:v2p144/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r3.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r3.claim: Al-Rāghib derives answering from cutting the gap between a speaker's mouth and listener's ear; the author instead regards that as figurative penetration and decisive resolution.
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r3.anchor: وقد ذهب "الراغب" إلى أنه جاء "من قطع الفجوة بين فم المجيب إلى أذن السامع".

BINTSHATI:v2p144/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r4.claim: Jābū means they cut through the rock; the author rejects other senses and takes this as evidence of Thamūd's strength in carving rock in the valley, where they lived until the blast.
BINTSHATI:v2p144/r4.anchor: ولا نرى حملها على غير معناها من القطع والنفاذ

BINTSHATI:v2p145/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p145/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p145/r1.claim: The Qur'anic valley references include ʿĀd's valleys in al-Aḥqāf, Abraham's dry valley home, the valley of Solomon's ants, and the sacred valley where God addressed Moses.

BINTSHATI:v2p146/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI:v2p146/r3.speaker: author
BINTSHATI:v2p146/r3.claim: The Prophet and his unlettered people knew no earlier histories beyond revelation; Hūd 49 says these are unseen reports, so the later extravagant tales are Israelite legends inserted into Qur'anic exegesis.
BINTSHATI:v2p146/r3.anchor: فمن أين جاءت كل هاتيك التفصيلات والحكايات التي حشيت بها كتب التفسير

BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r1.claim: The discussion moves from Ad to the nearer and similar Thamud, who received gardens and crops but answered divine favor with disbelief and preferred blindness; their she-camel was a clear sign of power.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r1.anchor: ثنى بأقرب الأمم إليهم زمانا وأشبههم بهم شأنا

BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r2.claim: Thamud cut through rock in the Valley of al-Hijr or Wadi al-Qura and carved mountain houses as if defying time.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r2.anchor: نقبوا وقطعوا قطعا حقيقا كأنه عندهم كالواجب

BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r3.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r3.claim: Abu Hayyan says Thamud were the first to carve mountains, rocks, and marble, and built 1,700 stone cities.
BIQAI-FULL:v8p417/r3.anchor: قال أبو حيان : قيل أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام ثمود

DURR-FULL:v8p506/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p506/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p506/r4.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Thamūd carved houses in mountains and Pharaoh’s stakes were the troops who built up his power.
DURR-FULL:v8p506/r4.anchor: عن عباس في قوله: {جابوا الصخر بالواد} قال: كانوا ينحتون من الجبال بيوتا

DURR-FULL:v8p506/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p506/r5.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR-FULL:v8p506/r5.claim: In a question from Nāfiʿ ibn al-Azraq, Ibn ʿAbbās defines “they cut through rock” as boring into mountain stone to make homes, citing Umayya’s use of *jāba* for piercing.
DURR-FULL:v8p506/r5.anchor: عن ابن عباس إن نافع بن الأزرق سأله عن قوله: {جابوا الصخر} قال نقبوا الحجارة في الجبال

DURR-FULL:v8p506/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v8p506/r6.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v8p506/r6.claim: Mujāhid says Thamūd hollowed the mountains into houses and Pharaoh drove people to stakes.
DURR-FULL:v8p506/r6.anchor: عن مجاهد {جابوا الصخر} قال: حرقوا الجبال فجعلوها بيوتا {وفرعون ذي الأوتاد} قال: كان يتد الناس

TAB:89:9/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:9/r1.speaker: author
TAB:89:9/r1.claim: Thamud cut through rock and made it into dwellings, as another verse says they carved houses in the mountains.
TAB:89:9/r1.anchor: وبثمود الذي خرقوا الصخر ودخلوه ، فاتخذوه بيوتا

TAB:89:9/r2.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:9/r2.speaker: author
TAB:89:9/r2.claim: The verb jāba means to enter and cut across a place; al-Tabari supports this sense with al-Nabigha’s use of yajūbu.
TAB:89:9/r2.anchor: ومنه قول نابغة : أتاكَ أبُو لَيْلَى يجُوبُ بِهِ الدّجَى

TAB:89:9/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:9/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:9/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses the phrase as piercing through the rock.
TAB:89:9/r3.anchor: عن ابن عباس ، في قوله : وَثَمُودَ الّذِينَ جابُوا الصّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ يقول : فخرقوها

TAB:89:9/r4.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:9/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
TAB:89:9/r4.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies them as Salih’s Thamud, who carved houses out of mountains.
TAB:89:9/r4.anchor: عن ابن عباس : وَثَمُودَ الّذِينَ جابُوا الصّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ يعني : ثمود قوم صالح

TAB:89:9/r5.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:9/r5.speaker: مجاهد
TAB:89:9/r5.claim: Mujahid says they cut into the mountains and made them into homes.
TAB:89:9/r5.anchor: عن مجاهد في قوله : الّذِينَ جابُوا الصّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ قال : جابوا الجبال ، فجعلوها بيوتا

TAB:89:9/r6.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:9/r6.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:9/r6.claim: Qatada says they cut through and carved the rock into houses.
TAB:89:9/r6.anchor: عن قتادة قوله : وَثَمُودَ الّذِينَ جابُوا الصّخْرَ بالْوَادِ : جابوها ونحتوها بيوتا

TAB:89:9/r7.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:9/r7.speaker: قتادة
TAB:89:9/r7.claim: Qatada also glosses the phrase as boring through the rock.
TAB:89:9/r7.anchor: عن قتادة ، قال : جابُوا الصّخْرَ قال : نَقَبوا الصخر

TAB:89:9/r8.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:9/r8.speaker: الضحاك
TAB:89:9/r8.claim: Al-Dahhak glosses the phrase as hewing stones.
TAB:89:9/r8.anchor: سمعت الضحاك يقول في قوله : جابُوا الصّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ يقول : قَدّوا الحجارة

TAB:89:9/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:9/r9.speaker: ابن زيد
TAB:89:9/r9.claim: Ibn Zayd says they made dwellings in mountain rock, hollowing it out for homes.
TAB:89:9/r9.anchor: قال ابن زيد ، في قوله : الّذِينَ جابُوا الصّخْرَ بِالْوَادِ : ضربوا البيوت والمساكن في الصخر في الجبال

TAB:89:9/r10.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB:89:9/r10.speaker: قائل غير مسمى
TAB:89:9/r10.claim: An anonymous couplet following Ibn Zayd’s gloss evokes people building in hard rock with powerful arms as evidence for the account.
TAB:89:9/r10.anchor: قال قائل : ألا كُلّ شَيْءٍ ما خَلا اللّهَ بائِدٌ *** كمَا بادَ حَيّ مِنْ شَنِيقٍ وَمارِدِ هُمُ ضَرَبُوا فِي كُلّ صَلاّءَ صَعْدَةٍ *** بأيْدٍ شِدَادٍ أيّدَاتِ السّوَاعِدِ

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r1.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r1.claim: Majāz does not apply to homonyms with no relation between their senses, such as thawr for a large piece of curd or day and night for bird names.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r1.anchor: لم يجز استعماله في الألفاظ التي يقع فيها اشتراك من غير سبب يكون بين المشتركين

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r2.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r2.claim: The verse-like wordplay “I ate the day at noon and night on a dark night” illustrates direct, unrelated homonymous uses rather than a motivated metaphor.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r2.anchor: أكلت النهار بنصف النهار وليلا أكلت بليل بهيم

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r3.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r3.claim: Majāz signals that a word has an original conventional sense and is transferred to a second sense; proper names are called transferred, not metaphorical, even when derived from nouns, qualities, verbs, or sounds.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r3.anchor: أن للفظ أصلا مبدوءا به في الوضع ومقصودا وإن جريه على الثاني إنما هو على سبيل النقل

JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r4.author: ʿAbd al-Qāhir al-Jurjānī
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r4.speaker: author
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r4.claim: Transfer is figurative when interpretation supplies a relation, such as a container for its bearer, a part for a whole, a scout as an eye, or rain and sky for the plants and water they cause.
JURJANI-ASRAR:v1p343/r4.anchor: كتسميتهم الرجل عينا إذا كان ربيئة والناقة نابا ولا كما بين النبت والغيث وبين السماء والمطر

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p573/r1.claim: The preceding discussion says cutting conveys decisive penetration; of Thamud's cutting, the hard rock seems to have yielded to them, displaying their strength and the inhabited homes they built before the blast.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the Thamud as boring into rocks and mountains to make houses.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r6.anchor: فقال ابن عباس: نقبوا الحجارة والجبال فاتخذوها بيوتًا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r7.speaker: أمية
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r7.claim: Umayya's poem uses the verb for piercing the ears, supporting the sense of boring through rock.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r7.anchor: وشاهده قول أمية! وشق أبصارنا كيما نعيش بها. . . وجاب للسمع أصماخاً وآذاناً

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r8.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r8.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r8.claim: This form and use of jabu occurs only once in the Qur'an.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p571/r8.anchor: السؤال عن: جَابُوا، وحيدة فى القرآن بصيغتها واستعمالها

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p270/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p270/r1.speaker: الفراء
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p270/r1.claim: Al-Farra' and Ibn Sinan al-Khafaji say the final weak letters in yasri and bi-l-wadi were deleted to match the verse endings.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p270/r1.anchor: صرح "الفراء" في (معاني القرآن) بأن ياء العلة حذفت من: يسرِ (ى) لمشاكلة رءوس الآيات. وكذلك ذهب "ابن سنان الخفاجي"

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p270/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p270/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p270/r2.claim: She rejects rhyme as the purpose of deletion: the Qur'an also omits weak letters inside clauses and connected speech, as shown by al-Dani's examples at 11:105, 17:11, 54:6, 54:8, 50:41, 79:15–16, 28:30, and 20:12.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p270/r2.anchor: ويكفي الرد على من ذهبوا إلى حذف الياءين في آيات الفجر، لرعاية الفاصلة، أن نذكر أن القرآن الكريم لم يقتصر على حذفهما عنا في مقاطع الآيات

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r1.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās’s interpretation, close to al-Ṭabarī’s, is that the Thamūd bored, carved, and tunneled through rock to make homes.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r1.anchor: وما قاله ابن عباس في (جابوا الصخر) هو نحو ما في تأويل الطبري: خرقوا الصخر ونحتوه ونقبوه، واتخذوه بيوتا

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r2.speaker: قيل
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r2.claim: Another reported interpretation is that they crossed or cut through the valley.

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r3.speaker: قيل
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r3.claim: A further interpretation is that they split rock into a valley that could store water for their needs, a feat requiring strength and understanding.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r3.anchor: وقيل: بل معناه أنهم شقوا الصخر واتخذوه واديًا يخزنون فيه الماء لمنافعهم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r4.claim: The root j-w-b fundamentally conveys cutting; jāba can mean crossing a valley, and jawba denotes a hollow or gap.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r4.anchor: والجوب، بمعنى القطع، أصل في الدلالة: جاب الثوب قطعه، والجوب: درع يقطع للمرأة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r5.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r5.speaker: الراغب
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r5.claim: Al-Rāghib explains an answer as cutting the gap between the respondent’s mouth and the listener’s ear.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r5.anchor: ويذهب الراغب إلى أنه قطع الفجوة بين فم المجيب إلى أذن السامع

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r6.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r6.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r6.claim: The author rejects al-Rāghib’s account as implausible and prefers a figurative sense of cutting associated with answering.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r6.anchor: والأولى عندنا أن يكون قطعًا مجازيا بما يلتمس فيه من إجابة

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r7.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r7.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r7.claim: The Qur’an uses naqb in 50:36 and multiple forms of qaṭʿ; the author’s earlier reading of naqb finds an added sense of inspection and searching.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p572/r7.anchor: وسبق من تدبر النقب في السؤال عن: (فنقبوا في البلاد) أن في التنقيب دلالة الفحص والبحث

YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r10.author: Yumnā Ṭarīf al-Khūlī
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r10.speaker: author
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r10.claim: In collective memory, pre-revelation history survives either as condemned examples of tyranny and idolatry or as faded figures such as Pharaoh, Iram, and Thamūd.
YKHULI-TAJDID:c2/r10.anchor: خيالات باهتة وأمساخ شائهة لفرعون الجبار، وإرم ذات العماد، وثمود الذين جابوا الصخر بالواد

NASHR:v2p399#2/r14.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p399#2/r14.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p399#2/r14.claim: For بالواد, Warsh retains the yāʾ in connected reading, Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb in both positions, and Qunbul differs at pause.
NASHR:v2p399#2/r14.anchor: بالواد أثبتها وصلا ورش، وفي الحالين يعقوب وابن كثير بخلاف عن قنبل في الوقف

NASHR:v2p143/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p143/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p143/r2.claim: Letters omitted in connected recitation to avoid two adjacent sukūns but retained in the script are restored by all readers at pause, including the alif in جابوا الصخر.
NASHR:v2p143/r2.anchor: ومن المتفق عليه ما حذف من الياءات والواوات والألفات لالتقاء الساكنين، وهو ثابت رسما نحو: يؤتي الحكمة

NASHR:v2p191/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p191/r4.speaker: author
NASHR:v2p191/r4.claim: Warsh retains the yāʾ of بالواد in connection, while Ibn Kathīr and Yaʿqūb retain it both connected and at pause; most reports from Qunbul delete it at pause.
NASHR:v2p191/r4.anchor: فوافقه على إثباتها وصلا ورش، وفي الحالين ابن كثير، واختلف عن قنبل عنه في الوقف،

ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r1.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r1.claim: Jāba means to pierce or cut; jāba the lands means to traverse them, as the cited, unnamed poem illustrates.
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r1.anchor: جاب : خرق وقطع ، تقول جبت البلاد أجوبها ، إذا قطعتها وجاوزتها

ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r2.speaker: الشاعر
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r2.claim: The unnamed cited poem uses jābat for traversing a land.
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r2.anchor: ولا رأيت قلوصاً قبلها حملت *** ستين وسقاً ولا جابت بها بلدا

ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r3.speaker: ابن وثاب
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r3.claim: Ibn Waththāb reads Thamūd with tanwīn, while the majority leave it diptote.
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r3.anchor: وقرأ ابن وثاب وثمود بالتنوين . والجمهور : بمنع الصرف .

ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r4.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r4.claim: They cut and hollowed rock to make dwellings, as in the verse about carving houses from mountains.
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r4.anchor: { جابوا الصخر } : خرقوه ونحتوه ، فاتخذوا في الحجارة منها بيوتاً ، كما قال تعالى : { وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتاً }

ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r5.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r5.claim: One report says Thamūd first carved mountains, rocks, and marble, then built 1,700 stone cities in Wādī al-Qurā.
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r5.anchor: قيل : أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام ثمود ، وبنوا ألفاً وسبعمائة مدينة كلها بالحجارة بالوادي ، وادي القرى .

ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r6.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r6.claim: Another view says they cut through their valley and brought water in cleft rock, displaying strength and ambition.
ABUHAYYAN:89:9/r6.anchor: وقيل : جابوا واديهم وجلبوا ماءهم في صخر شقوه فعل ذي القوة والآمال .

ALUSI:89:9/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r1.claim: Thamūd is coordinated with ʿĀd; it is a well-known tribe named after its ancestor Thamūd, brother of Jadīs.
ALUSI:89:9/r1.anchor: وهي قبيلة مشهورة سميت باسم جدهم ثمود أخي جديس

ALUSI:89:9/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r2.claim: The genealogy given makes Thamūd and Jadīs sons of ʿĀbir ibn Iram ibn Sām ibn Noah.
ALUSI:89:9/r2.anchor: وهما ابنا عابر بن ارم بن سام بن نوح عليه السلام

ALUSI:89:9/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r3.claim: They were Arab peoples of ancient stock who lived at al-Ḥijr between the Hijaz and Tabuk and worshipped idols.
ALUSI:89:9/r3.anchor: كانوا عربا من العاربة يسكنون الحجر بين الحجاز وتبوك وكانوا يعبدون الأصنام

ALUSI:89:9/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r4.claim: Thamūd is normally diptote as a feminine proper name; Ibn Waththāb reads it with tanwīn, declining it as a people or clan.
ALUSI:89:9/r4.anchor: ومنع الصرف للعلمية والتأنيث وقرأ ابن وثاب بالتنوين صرفه باعتبار الحي

ALUSI:89:9/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r5.claim: One derivation treats Thamūd as Arabic from thamd, scant water without a replenishing source; mithmūd can describe women who exhaust a man's fluid or someone whose wealth is depleted by requests.
ALUSI:89:9/r5.anchor: فقيل هو فعول من الثمد وهو الماء القليل الذي لا مادة له

ALUSI:89:9/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r6.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI:89:9/r6.claim: Al-Rāghib instead says the name is foreign, explaining its diptote form through foreignness and proper-name status.
ALUSI:89:9/r6.anchor: وحكى الراغب أنه عجمي فمنع الصرف للعلمية والعجمية

ALUSI:89:9/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r7.claim: They cut into mountain rock and made houses by carving them, as in the parallel description at 26:149.
ALUSI:89:9/r7.anchor: أي قطعوا صخر الجبال واتخذوا فيها بيوتا نحتوها من الصخر

ALUSI:89:9/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r8.speaker: قيل
ALUSI:89:9/r8.claim: A report says Thamūd first carved stone, rock, and marble and built 1,700 stone cities; al-Ālūsī doubts the accuracy of the building claim.
ALUSI:89:9/r8.anchor: قيل أول من نحت الحجارة والصخور والرخام ثمود وبنوا ألفا وسبعمائة مدينة

ALUSI:89:9/r9.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r9.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r9.claim: The valley named is Wādī al-Qurā.
ALUSI:89:9/r9.anchor: هو وادي القرى وقرىء بالياء آخر الحروف

ALUSI:89:9/r10.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r10.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r10.claim: An unassigned reading adds a final yāʾ, reading al-wādī.

ALUSI:89:9/r11.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r11.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r11.claim: The bāʾ may mark location, with the phrase attached to jābū or made a circumstantial phrase modifying its subject or object.
ALUSI:89:9/r11.anchor: والباء للظرفية والجار والمجرور متعلق بجابوا أو بمحذوف هو حال من الفاعل أو المفعول

ALUSI:89:9/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r12.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r12.claim: Alternatively, bāʾ marks instrument or cause: they cut rock in their valley or because it was their valley, a place for water and an arena for the powerful; al-Ālūsī calls this contrary to the apparent sense.
ALUSI:89:9/r12.anchor: وقيل الباء للآلة أو السببية متعلقة بجابوا أي جابوا الصخر بواديهم أو بسببه

ALUSI:89:9/r13.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r13.speaker: author
ALUSI:89:9/r13.claim: Jābū means cut through; the apparent sense is literal, as in jābtu al-bilād, I traversed the lands.
ALUSI:89:9/r13.anchor: والظاهر أنه حقيقة فيه تقول جبت البلاد أجوبها إذا قطعتها

ALUSI:89:9/r14.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r14.speaker: شاعر
ALUSI:89:9/r14.claim: An unnamed poet's line uses jābat for traversing a country, evidencing this lexical sense.

ALUSI:89:9/r15.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI:89:9/r15.speaker: الراغب
ALUSI:89:9/r15.claim: Al-Rāghib derives jawb from cutting across a hollow in the land, then extends it to traversing any land; jawāb is called a reply because it bridges speaker and listener and became specialized for a response.
ALUSI:89:9/r15.anchor: وقال الراغب الجوب قطع الجوبة وهي الغائط من الأرض ثم يستعمل في قطع كل أرض

BAGHAWI:89:9/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:9/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:9/r1.claim: The conjunction means “and by Thamud,” carrying the oath preposition over to Thamud.
BAGHAWI:89:9/r1.anchor: أي : وبثمود ،   { الذين جابوا الصخر } قطعوا الحجر

BAGHAWI:89:9/r2.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:9/r2.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:9/r2.claim: They cut stone; صخرة is the singular form, and the people of Wadi al-Qura cut mountains into dwellings.
BAGHAWI:89:9/r2.anchor: جابوا الصخر } قطعوا الحجر ،   واحدتها : صخرة

BAGHAWI:89:9/r3.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:9/r3.speaker: author
BAGHAWI:89:9/r3.claim: The valley is Wadi al-Qura, where Thamud carved houses into the mountains.
BAGHAWI:89:9/r3.anchor: يعني : وادي القرى كانوا يقطعون الجبال فيجعلون فيها بيوتاً

BAGHAWI:89:9/r4.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:9/r4.speaker: ابن كثير ويعقوب
BAGHAWI:89:9/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir and Yaqub retain the final yāʾ of al-wādī in both connected and paused reading, preserving the original form.
BAGHAWI:89:9/r4.anchor: وأثبت ابن كثير ويعقوب الياء في الوادي وصلا ووقفاً على الأصل

BAGHAWI:89:9/r5.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:9/r5.speaker: ورش
BAGHAWI:89:9/r5.claim: Warsh retains the yāʾ in connected recitation only.

BAGHAWI:89:9/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI:89:9/r6.speaker: الآخرون
BAGHAWI:89:9/r6.claim: The other readers omit the yāʾ in both connected and paused recitation, matching the verse endings.
BAGHAWI:89:9/r6.anchor: والآخرون بحذفها في الحالين على وفق رؤوس الآي

BAYDAWI:89:9/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI:89:9/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI:89:9/r1.claim: Thamūd cut through rock and made dwellings from it, as 26:149 says of carving houses in mountains.
BAYDAWI:89:9/r1.anchor: قطعوه واتخذوه منازل لقوله وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا

BIQAI:89:9/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:9/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:9/r1.claim: After ʿĀd, whose case was more astonishing and story more unusual, the sūra turns to the Thamūd, nearer in time and similar in their circumstances.
BIQAI:89:9/r1.anchor: ولما بدأ بهؤلاء لأن أمرهم كان أعجب ، وقصتهم أنزه وأغرب ، ثنى بأقرب الأمم إليهم

BIQAI:89:9/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:9/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:9/r2.claim: Thamūd enjoyed gardens, springs, crops, and dates with tender clusters, yet answered these gifts and the miraculous she-camel, a sign of divine power, with disbelief rather than gratitude and chose blindness over guidance.
BIQAI:89:9/r2.anchor: فجعلوا موضع ما لزمهم من الشكر الكفر

BIQAI:89:9/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:9/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:9/r3.claim: Jābū means they pierced and cut through the rock literally, as though the act were incumbent upon them.
BIQAI:89:9/r3.anchor: أي نقبوا وقطعوا قطعاً حقيقياً كأنه عندهم كالواجب

BIQAI:89:9/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:9/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:9/r4.claim: The valley is identified either as Wādī al-Ḥijr or Wādī al-Qurā.
BIQAI:89:9/r4.anchor: أي وادي الحجر أو وادي القرى

BIQAI:89:9/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:9/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI:89:9/r5.claim: They made dwellings cut into mountains, as if trying to outlast and defeat time.
BIQAI:89:9/r5.anchor: فجعلوا بيوتاً منقورة في الجبال فعل من يغتال الدهر ويفني الزمان

BIQAI:89:9/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI:89:9/r6.speaker: أبو حيان
BIQAI:89:9/r6.claim: Abū Ḥayyān cites the view that Thamūd were the first to carve mountains, rocks, and marble, and that they built 1,700 stone cities.
BIQAI:89:9/r6.anchor: قال أبو حيان : قيل أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام ثمود

DURR:89:9/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:9/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:9/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas says Thamud carved houses from mountains; Pharaoh's pegs were the soldiers who strengthened his rule.
DURR:89:9/r1.anchor: عن ابن عباس في قوله : { جابوا الصخر بالواد } قال : كانوا ينحتون من الجبال بيوتاً

DURR:89:9/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:9/r2.speaker: ابن عباس
DURR:89:9/r2.claim: To Nafi ibn al-Azraq, Ibn Abbas glosses jabu as piercing mountain stone to make homes.
DURR:89:9/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس أن نافع بن الأزرق سأله

DURR:89:9/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:9/r3.speaker: أمية
DURR:89:9/r3.claim: Ibn Abbas cites Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's poem, whose use of jaba for boring through the ear witnesses the Arabic sense of piercing or hollowing.
DURR:89:9/r3.anchor: قول أمية : وشق أبصارنا كيما نعيش بها *** وجاب للسمع أصماخاً وآذاناً

DURR:89:9/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR:89:9/r4.speaker: مجاهد
DURR:89:9/r4.claim: Mujahid offers a different account: Thamud burned the mountains and made them into houses.
DURR:89:9/r4.anchor: عن مجاهد { جابوا الصخر } قال : حرقوا الجبال فجعلوها بيوتاً

IBNASHUR:89:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:9/r1.claim: Thamud is diptote because it names the known people; the masculine plural relative pronoun treats them as a people, then shifts from the expected feminine form for stylistic variation.
IBNASHUR:89:9/r1.anchor: ومنع { ثمود } من الصرف لأن المراد به الأمة المعروفة ، ووصف باسم الموصول لجمع المذكّر

IBNASHUR:89:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:9/r2.claim: Jab means to cut through: the Thamud carved houses in rock, as also described at 26:149.
IBNASHUR:89:9/r2.anchor: ومعنى { جابوا } : قطعوا ، أي نحتوا الصخر واتخذوا فيه بيوتاً كما قال تعالى : { وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتاً } [ الشعراء : 149 ]

IBNASHUR:89:9/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:9/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:9/r3.claim: Ibn Ashur notes the claim that Thamud were the first human community to carve stone and marble.
IBNASHUR:89:9/r3.anchor: وقد قيل : إن ثمود أول أمم البشر نحتوا الصخر والرخام

IBNASHUR:89:9/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:9/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:9/r5.claim: Wadi first denotes low ground between two mountains and then a substantial watercourse; its ending may be dāl or a quiescent yāʾ after dāl.
IBNASHUR:89:9/r5.anchor: والواد : اسم لأرض كائنة بين جبلين منخفضة ، ومنه سمي مجرى الماء الكثير واداً وفيه لغتان

IBNASHUR:89:9/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:9/r6.speaker: الجمهور وابن كثير ويعقوب وورش عن نافع
IBNASHUR:89:9/r6.claim: The majority read without final yāʾ; Ibn Kathir and Yaqub retain it in pause and liaison, while Warsh from Nafiʿ retains it only in liaison, following the rhyme pattern as at 89:4. The rasm omits yāʾ, but readings depend on oral transmission, with the mushaf serving as a memory aid.
IBNASHUR:89:9/r6.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور بدون ياء . وقرأه ابن كثير ويعقوب بياء في آخره

IBNASHUR:89:9/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:9/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:9/r7.claim: Al-Wadi is the conventional name for Thamud’s homes, also called Wadi al-Qura, al-Hijr, or Hijr Thamud; it lies between Khaybar and Tayma on the Medina–Syria route.
IBNASHUR:89:9/r7.anchor: والواد : علَم بالغلبة على منازل ثمود ، ويقال له : وادي القُرى

IBNASHUR:89:9/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:9/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:9/r8.claim: After Thamud, Jews settled the valley when they came to Arabia; later Arab groups there included Qudaʿah, Juhaynah, ʿUdhrah, and Bali.
IBNASHUR:89:9/r8.anchor: ونزله اليهود بعد ثمود لما نزلوا بلاد العرب

IBNASHUR:89:9/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:9/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:9/r9.claim: The Prophet campaigned there and captured it in year seven; its Arabs accepted Islam and its Jews made a treaty to pay jizya.
IBNASHUR:89:9/r9.anchor: وكان غزاه النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وفتحه سنة سبع فأسلم من فيه من العرب

IBNASHUR:89:9/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR:89:9/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR:89:9/r10.claim: The preposition bi in bi-l-wadi is locative.

IBNATIYYA:89:9/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r1.speaker: يحيى بن وثاب
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r1.claim: Yahya ibn Waththab reads Thamūd with tanwīn on the dāl.
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r1.anchor: وقرأ يحيى بن وثاب «وثموداً » بتنوين الدال ،

IBNATIYYA:89:9/r2.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r2.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r2.claim: Jābū al-ṣakhr means they cut through and carved rock; the Thamud carved homes into the stone of their valleys.
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r2.anchor: معناه خرقوه ونحتوه ، وكانوا في أوديتهم قد نحتوا بيوتهم في حجارة

IBNATIYYA:89:9/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r3.claim: A wādī is the space between two mountains, whether or not water runs through it.
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r3.anchor: ما بين الجبلين وإن لم يكن فيه ماء

IBNATIYYA:89:9/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r4.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r4.claim: Many commentators understand the phrase as the Thamud carving their houses from stone in their valleys.
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r4.anchor: هذا قول كثير من المفسرين في معنى { جابوا الصخر بالواد }

IBNATIYYA:89:9/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r5.speaker: الثعلبي
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r5.claim: Al-Tha'labi specifies the valley as Wadi al-Qura.

IBNATIYYA:89:9/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r6.speaker: قوم
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r6.claim: Another group says they cut into their valley and brought water through split rock, an act showing strength and ambition.
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r6.anchor: وقال قوم : المعنى جابوا واديهم وجلبوا ماءهم في صخر شقوه ، وهذا فعل ذوي القوة والآمال

IBNATIYYA:89:9/r7.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r7.speaker: ابن كثير وأكثر السبعة ونافع
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir reads al-wādī with a yāʾ; most of the Seven read al-wād without it, and Nafi's reading is disputed.
IBNATIYYA:89:9/r7.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير بالوادي «بياء ، وقرأ أكثر السبعة » بالواد «ياء واختلف في ذلك نافع

IBNKATHIR:89:9/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r1.claim: Thamūd cut through stone in the valley.
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r1.anchor: يعني : يقطعون الصخر بالوادي . قال ابن عباس

IBNKATHIR:89:9/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r2.speaker: ابن عباس ومجاهد وقتادة والضحاك وابن زيد
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says they carved and bored into the rock; Mujāhid, Qatāda, al-Ḍaḥḥāk, and Ibn Zayd agree.
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r2.anchor: قال ابن عباس : ينحتونها ويخرقونها . وكذا قال مجاهد ، وقتادة ، والضحاك ، وابن زيد

IBNKATHIR:89:9/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r3.claim: The idiom “mujtābī al-nimār” means those who tore them; “ijtāba a garment” means to open it, as with the garment’s neck-opening (jayb).
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r3.anchor: اجتاب الثوب : إذا فتحه . ومنه الجيب أيضا

IBNKATHIR:89:9/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r4.claim: The account is linked to 26:149, where Thamūd are said to hew houses from mountains.
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r4.anchor: وقال الله تعالى : { وَتَنْحِتُونَ مِنَ الْجِبَالِ بُيُوتًا فَارِهِينَ }

IBNKATHIR:89:9/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r5.speaker: شاعر غير مسمى
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r5.claim: Ibn Kathir cites an unnamed poet’s couplet, whose second line describes striking hard rock with strong arms, as evidence for the stone-cutting sense.
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r5.anchor:
أنشد ابن جرير وابن أبي حاتم هاهنا قول الشاعر :
ألا كل شيء - ما خلا الله – بائد

IBNKATHIR:89:9/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r6.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r6.claim: Ibn Isḥāq says Thamūd were Arabs whose home was Wādī al-Qurā.
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r6.anchor: وقال ابن إسحاق : كانوا عربا ، وكان منزلهم بوادي القرى

IBNKATHIR:89:9/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r7.claim: Ibn Kathir says the detailed account of ʿĀd was already given in Sūrat al-Aʿrāf, so he does not repeat it here.
IBNKATHIR:89:9/r7.anchor: وقد ذكرنا قصة " عاد " مستقصاة في سورة " الأعراف " بما أغنى عن إعادته

MAWARDI:89:9/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:9/r1.speaker: author
