MAWARDI:89:9/r1.claim: The Thamūd cut, bored, and carved rock into houses; the cited verse about carving mountain homes and a poet's line support this sense.
MAWARDI:89:9/r1.anchor: أحدهما : يعني قطعوا الصخر ونقبوه ونحتوه حتى جعلوه بيوتاً ،   كما قال تعالى

MAWARDI:89:9/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:9/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI:89:9/r2.claim: Alternatively, they traveled through the valley to take rock, as a cited poet's line about carrying a camel-load through a land illustrates.
MAWARDI:89:9/r2.anchor: الثاني : معناه طافوا لأخذ الصخر بالوادي ،   كما قال الشاعر

MAWARDI:89:9/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:9/r3.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
MAWARDI:89:9/r3.claim: Ibn Isḥāq identifies the valley as Wādī al-Qurā.
MAWARDI:89:9/r3.anchor: فقد زعم محمد بن إسحاق أنه وادي القرى ،   وروى أبو الأشهب

MAWARDI:89:9/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI:89:9/r4.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI:89:9/r4.claim: Abū al-Ashhab reports from Abū Naḍra that during the Tabūk expedition the Prophet passed through Thamūd's valley and told the party to hurry because it was a cursed valley.
MAWARDI:89:9/r4.anchor: وروى أبو الأشهب عن أبي نضرة قال : أتى رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم

NASAFI:89:9/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI:89:9/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI:89:9/r1.claim: Thamud cut into mountain rock to make houses; the passage says they were the first to carve mountains and stones and built 1,700 cities, all of stone, in Wadi al-Qura.
NASAFI:89:9/r1.anchor: { وَثَمُودَ الذين جَابُواْ الصخر } قطعوا صخر الجبال واتخذوا فيها بيوتا . قيل : أول من نحت الجبال والصخور ثمود

QURTUBI:89:9/r1.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:9/r1.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:9/r1.claim: Thamud are the people of the prophet Salih.

QURTUBI:89:9/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:9/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:9/r2.claim: The verb means they cut through or traversed; the shirt opening is named because it is cut.
QURTUBI:89:9/r2.anchor: " جابوا " : قطعوا . ومنه : فلان يجوب البلاد ، أي يقطعها . وإنما سمي جيب القميص لأنه جيب . أي قطع

QURTUBI:89:9/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:9/r3.speaker: الشاعر
QURTUBI:89:9/r3.claim: An unnamed poet uses جابت for a camel traversing a land while carrying sixty wasqs, illustrating the verb's sense.
QURTUBI:89:9/r3.anchor: ستين وسقا ولا جابت به بلدا أي قطعت

QURTUBI:89:9/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:9/r4.speaker: المفسرون
QURTUBI:89:9/r4.claim: Commentators say Thamud were the first to carve mountains, images, and marble; they built 1,700 stone cities and 2,700,000 stone houses.
QURTUBI:89:9/r4.anchor: قال المفسرون : أول من نحت الجبال والصور والرخام : ثمود . فبنوا من المدائن ألفا وسبعمائة مدينة كلها من الحجارة

QURTUBI:89:9/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:9/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:9/r5.claim: Because of their strength, they extracted rocks, tunneled into mountains, and made houses for themselves.
QURTUBI:89:9/r5.anchor: وكانوا لقوتهم يخرجون الصخور ، وينقبون الجبال ، ويجعلونها بيوتا لأنفسهم

QURTUBI:89:9/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:9/r6.speaker: محمد بن إسحاق
QURTUBI:89:9/r6.claim: Ibn Ishaq identifies the valley as Wadi al-Qura.
QURTUBI:89:9/r6.anchor: " بالوادي " أي بوادي القرى . قاله محمد بن إسحاق

QURTUBI:89:9/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:9/r7.speaker: أبو نضرة
QURTUBI:89:9/r7.claim: Abu Nadhra reports that during the Tabuk expedition the Prophet, passing through the valley of Thamud, ordered the army to hurry because it was a cursed valley.
QURTUBI:89:9/r7.anchor: أبي نضرة قال : أتى رسول اللّه صلى اللّه عليه وسلم في غزاة تبوك

QURTUBI:89:9/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:9/r8.speaker: قيل
QURTUBI:89:9/r8.claim: Another description says the valley lies between mountains, where Thamud tunneled homes, dwellings, and cisterns.
QURTUBI:89:9/r8.anchor: وقيل : الوادي بين جبال ، وكانوا ينقبون في تلك الجبال بيوتا ودورا وأحواضا

QURTUBI:89:9/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI:89:9/r9.speaker: author
QURTUBI:89:9/r9.claim: A valley is any opening between mountains or hills that serves as a route and outlet for flowing water.
QURTUBI:89:9/r9.anchor: وكل منفرج بين جبال أو تلال يكون مسلكا للسيل ومنفذا فهو واد

RAZI:89:9/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:9/r1.speaker: الليث
RAZI:89:9/r1.claim: Al-Layth explains jawb as cutting through something, like cutting an opening in a garment.
RAZI:89:9/r1.anchor: قال الليث : الجواب قطعك الشيء كما يجاب الجيب

RAZI:89:9/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:9/r2.speaker: الفراء
RAZI:89:9/r2.claim: Al-Farrāʾ adds the form yajib jayban and says that traversing a country is called jawb.

RAZI:89:9/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:9/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI:89:9/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās says Thamūd cut through lands to make houses, pools, and whatever buildings they wanted.
RAZI:89:9/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس : كانوا يجوبون البلاد فيجعلون منها بيوتا

RAZI:89:9/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:9/r4.speaker: author
RAZI:89:9/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī links this account of carving rock dwellings to the Qurʾānic statement that they carved houses from mountains.
RAZI:89:9/r4.anchor: كما قال : { وتنحتون من الجبال بيوتا }

RAZI:89:9/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:9/r5.speaker: author
RAZI:89:9/r5.claim: An unattributed report says Thamūd were the first to quarry mountains, stone, and marble.
RAZI:89:9/r5.anchor: قيل : أول من نحت الجبال والصخور والرخام ثمود

RAZI:89:9/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:9/r6.speaker: author
RAZI:89:9/r6.claim: The same report says they built 1,700 cities, all of stone.
RAZI:89:9/r6.anchor: وبنوا ألفا وسبعمائة مدينة كلها من الحجارة

RAZI:89:9/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI:89:9/r7.speaker: مقاتل
RAZI:89:9/r7.claim: Muqātil identifies the valley as Wādī al-Qurā.
